title: Streaming-aware invocation mediator for legacy function compatibility
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a streaming-aware invocation mediator that lets OpenAI-style tool calls interoperate with Redwood legacy function contracts without changing callers. The mediator should handle partial/streaming outputs, map streaming fragments into the legacy function parameter model, support multiple naming aliases, and provide runtime flags for gradual rollout and deprecation paths.
acceptance_criteria: 0) End-to-end integration tests validating streaming tool calls routed to legacy function backends pass in CI
1) Runtime can accept OpenAI-style tool descriptors and synthesize legacy function invocation payloads (including name mapping and parameter flattening)
2) Streaming responses from invoked tools are surfaced to callers as a normalized stream envelope, and legacy backends that require whole-payloads can opt-in to buffered delivery
3) Feature flag exists to enable the mediator per-customer and per-route for canarying
4) Telemetry metrics emitted: parse failures, buffer memory high-water marks, latency penalty when buffering, and fallback counts
technical_notes: Design two delivery modes: streaming-proxy (forward fragments as they arrive) and buffered-call (accumulate until termination then call legacy fn)

Introduce an alias registry that maps OpenAI-style tool 'name' + 'display_name' variants to canonical legacy function identifiers. Registry supports precedence rules and last-writer-wins backfill from import jobs
Use backpressure signals from runtime to prevent unbounded buffering; implement configurable memory cap per-invocation and graceful degrade to buffered-call failover
When streaming-proxy mode is used, attach frame metadata so legacy function logs can correlate partial fragments with a single invocation ID
Prefer in-memory streaming for sub-1MB workloads; for larger streams, spill fragments to ephemeral object store and pass reference to legacy backend
Compatibility mapping rules: parameter flattening, type coercion (string->json when necessary), and reserved-key stripping (redwood_* keys)
decisions: Keep mediator as a distinct runtime component instead of embedding in the router to allow independent scaling and rollout
Default mode will be streaming-proxy where possible; buffered-call only when legacy contract declares strict non-stream semantics or when fragment ordering semantics are required
Expose name-alias rules via Console UI and provide admin API to seed mappings for enterprise customers
risks: Increased latency for legacy backends when buffering is required; SLO regressions need mitigation and monitoring
Complexity around ordering and idempotency for partial fragments may surface new classes of bugs in legacy handlers
Memory pressure from high-concurrency streaming workloads if backpressure not tuned correctly
testing_plan: Unit tests for alias registry resolution and precedence logic
Integration tests exercising streaming-proxy -> legacy backend and buffered-call flows under synthetic load
Chaos tests: drop middle fragments, reorder frames, simulate slow consumers to validate backpressure/failover
Canary rollout to 5% of hosted customers with telemetry dashboard and automatic rollback on error rate spike
